verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission of NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket making its first crewed launch'; R2: 'NASA’s first mission with crew aboard the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and Orion spacecraft'; R5: 'Artemis II will be the first crewed mission of the Artemis programme'; R6: 'first crewed flight of NASA’s deep space exploration system, featuring the Orion spacecraft, the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Artemis II as the first crewed SLS and Orion mission, following uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch four astronauts around the Moon in early 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: Launch on 'April 1, 2026' with four astronauts (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen) to 'loop around [the moon]'; R5: 'By April 2026'; R6: 'around the Moon'; all sources confirm four astronauts and lunar flyby in 2026.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm launch in April 2026 (early 2026), four specific astronauts, and mission profile around the Moon.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first human lunar flight in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; R3: 'first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years', '54-year intermission'; R4: 'first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years'; R7: 'first U.S. human lunar spaceflight in over 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe it as the first crewed lunar mission since Apollo, over 50 years (52-54 years from 2026).

verifications.claim: Artemis II will test life support systems for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'check out all of (Orion's) environmental control, life support systems'; R3: 'check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey and keep its crew alive'; R6: 'life-support and environmental systems'; R7: 'test life-support systems in the Orion capsule for future crewed missions to the moon’s surface'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm testing of life support/environmental systems in Orion for future missions.
